questions.explain: Kıtalar hareket ediyor (doğru), ama 'do not plough through the seafloor; they ride on moving plates' (mekanizma yanlış). 'vindicated' = haklı çıkmak.

title: Chemicals That Refuse to Break Down
text:
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly known as PFAS, are a family of several thousand synthetic chemicals that have been produced since the 1940s. Their defining feature is the bond between carbon and fluorine, one of the strongest in organic chemistry. This bond gives PFAS remarkable properties: they repel both water and oil, withstand high temperatures and resist chemical attack. As a result, they have been used in non-stick cookware, waterproof clothing, food packaging and fire-fighting foams.

The very stability that makes PFAS so useful also makes them a problem. Because natural processes break them down extremely slowly, if at all, they have earned the nickname "forever chemicals". They have now been detected in rainwater, soil, wildlife and the blood of most people tested in industrialised countries. Some well-studied PFAS have been linked to effects on the immune system, raised cholesterol and certain cancers, which has prompted regulators to restrict them and to set increasingly strict limits for drinking water.

Removing PFAS once they are in the environment is difficult and expensive. Activated carbon filters and specialised resins can capture many of them from water, but this only transfers the chemicals to another material that must then be disposed of. Destroying them generally requires very high temperatures or energy-intensive treatments, and researchers are investigating methods that break the carbon-fluorine bond under milder conditions. Many scientists argue that, given the size of the chemical family, regulating substances one at a time is too slow. They propose treating PFAS as a single class and limiting their use to applications that are essential and for which no safer alternatives exist.

questions.q: According to the passage, the carbon-fluorine bond is responsible for ----.
options: both the useful properties of PFAS and their persistence in the environment
the low cost of fire-fighting foams
the rapid breakdown of PFAS in rainwater
the ability of PFAS to absorb water
the use of PFAS as a medicine
questions.explain: Bağ yararlı özellikleri veriyor; 'The very stability that makes PFAS so useful also makes them a problem'. Tuzak: suyu 'repel' eder, emmez.

questions.q: The author points out that filters and resins are not a complete solution because they ----.
options: only move the chemicals into another material that still needs disposal
cannot capture any PFAS from water
destroy the carbon-fluorine bond too quickly
require milder conditions than other methods
produce new forms of PFAS
questions.explain: 'this only transfers the chemicals to another material that must then be disposed of'.

questions.q: It can be inferred that the scientists mentioned in the last paragraph believe that ----.
options: all PFAS should be allowed in consumer products
PFAS pose no risk to human health
each PFAS should be studied for decades before any action
no applications of PFAS are essential
current substance-by-substance regulation cannot keep up with the number of PFAS
questions.explain: 'regulating substances one at a time is too slow' + sınıf olarak düzenleme önerisi. Tuzak: 'no applications are essential' — 'essential' kullanıma izin veriyorlar.

title: The Bridge That Danced
text:
When the Tacoma Narrows Bridge opened in the state of Washington in July 1940, it was the third-longest suspension bridge in the world and a showcase of elegant, economical design. Its deck was remarkably slender: instead of a deep, open steel truss, it was stiffened by shallow solid plate girders, which made it light and graceful but also unusually flexible. Even during construction, workers noticed that the deck moved up and down in moderate winds, and the bridge soon acquired the nickname "Galloping Gertie". Drivers sometimes crossed it for the thrill of watching cars ahead disappear and reappear in the waves of the roadway.

On 7 November 1940, only four months after opening, a steady wind of roughly 65 kilometres per hour set the deck into a violent twisting motion. For about an hour, the roadway rotated back and forth until cables and supports failed and the central span collapsed into the water below. Nobody was killed, although a dog trapped in an abandoned car was lost.

The collapse is often presented in textbooks as a simple case of resonance, in which the wind pushed the bridge at its natural frequency. Engineers now regard this explanation as incomplete. A steady wind does not supply a regular periodic push in the way that a child is pushed on a swing. Instead, the twisting motion of the deck altered the airflow around it, and the airflow in turn fed energy back into the motion, a self-excited phenomenon known as aeroelastic flutter. The failure transformed bridge engineering: designers began testing models in wind tunnels and favouring deeper or aerodynamically shaped decks, practices that remain standard today.

questions.q: According to the passage, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge was unusually flexible mainly because ----.
options: it was built with weak cables
it was the longest suspension bridge in the world
workers built it during strong winds
it was designed to move for the thrill of drivers
its deck was stiffened by shallow plate girders instead of a deep truss
questions.explain: 'stiffened by shallow solid plate girders, which made it light and graceful but also unusually flexible'. Tuzak: 'longest' — metin 'third-longest'.

questions.q: The author mentions a child on a swing in order to ----.
options: show that the bridge was designed for children
illustrate the kind of regular push that a steady wind does not provide
prove that resonance fully explains the collapse
describe how the cables were tested
compare the bridge's length with a playground
questions.explain: Salıncak periyodik itme örneği; yazar rüzgârın böyle itmediğini, rezonans açıklamasının eksik olduğunu gösteriyor.

questions.q: Which of the following can be concluded from the passage?
options: Engineers today consider resonance the complete explanation of the collapse.
The bridge collapsed on the day it opened.
The collapse led to lasting changes in the methods used to design bridges.
Several drivers were killed in the collapse.
Wind tunnel testing had been standard before 1940.
questions.explain: 'The failure transformed bridge engineering ... practices that remain standard today'. Tuzak: 'incomplete' açıklama; kimse ölmedi; 4 ay sonra çöktü.
